newsitem.title: CHINA: World Bank loans $2.97 bln to China in fiscal '96.
newsitem.headline: World Bank loans $2.97 bln to China in fiscal '96.

text.p: The World Bank's lending commitents to China reached $2.97 billion in fiscal year 1996 ending June 30, 1996, an official of the bank's mission in China said on Tuesday.
Of the loans, China would have to pay interest on $2.49 billion, the official told Reuters, adding that the remaining $480 million was interest free.
The interest rate was 7.07 percent between July 1 and December 31, 1995 and 6.98 percent between January 1 to June 30, 1996, the official said.
China became the top borrower from the World Bank in fiscal year 1993, she said.
The World Bank's loan commitments to China in fiscal year 1995 ending June 30, 1995 totalled $2.9995 billion, of which $630 million was interest free, she said.
China had to pay interest on the remaining $2.3695 billion. She did not give the interest rate.
